title: [platform] list_enterprise_source_stubs error keeps happening
body: I am deploying Airbyte on-prem for the first time with Helm chart 1.3.1. After the installation is clean, source and destination operations fail, and the airbyte-server log shows 403 responses while fetching the compatibility matrix and the connector registry entry for airbyte/source-easypost:0.0.1. I tried setting ENTERPRISE_SOURCE_STUBS_URL to an empty string in my Helm values, but the issue still occurs.

symptoms_visible: After deploying Helm chart 1.3.1, source and destination operations fail.
The airbyte-server log reports 403 responses while fetching the compatibility matrix and the connector registry entry for airbyte/source-easypost:0.0.1.
The same errors remain after I set ENTERPRISE_SOURCE_STUBS_URL to an empty string.
N0.label: N0 remote connector data errors reported

symptoms_visible: The errors occur on a first-time Airbyte installation rather than after an upgrade.
N1.label: N1 fresh installation confirmed

symptoms_visible: When I tested Helm chart 1.1.1, this problem did not occur; the deployment using 1.3.1 produced the errors.
N2.label: N2 older chart comparison

symptoms_visible: On affected later OSS deployments, opening the source list can return HTTP 500 from /api/v1/source_definitions/list_enterprise_source_stubs with 'HTTP error fetching enterprise sources'.
Restarting the airbyte-server pod did not restore source loading on every affected deployment.
N3.label: N3 recurring endpoint failure characterized

symptoms_visible: I have not reported whether source and destination creation works on my deployment after the endpoint correction, a server-pod restart, or an Airbyte update.
N_terminal.label: terminal maintainer fix reported without reporter retest

question_patterns: Is this a fresh deployment or an upgrade from an earlier Airbyte version?
Was chart 1.3.1 installed for the first time, or did you upgrade an existing deployment?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It is a first-time installation, not an upgrade.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: This started during an upgrade of a long-running deployment, and the old database and configuration were retained.
It is a fresh installation in a namespace that had previously been created but contained no Airbyte resources.

edges.comment: Opening reporter's deployment only; based on c0-c3. The reporter confirms that chart 1.3.1 was installed for the first time.

question_patterns: Can you compare this with an older chart deployment and report whether the same source and destination errors occur?
Does a test deployment using an earlier Helm chart show the same behavior?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested version 1.1.1, and this problem does not exist there.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same 403 and source-list errors also occur on chart 1.1.1.
The test used chart 1.1.0 instead, and source creation worked there.

solution.intent: Use an older chart deployment as a comparison to determine whether the failure is specific to the newer Airbyte packaging or remote-data path.
solution.concrete_example: Create a separate test deployment with an older chart and check whether opening the source and destination lists produces the same server errors.

edges.comment: Opening reporter's systems only; based on c4. Testing chart 1.1.1 installs another version and therefore creates S2 rather than being modeled as a measurement-only state.

question_patterns: Are affected OSS users seeing this same enterprise-source loading failure on later Airbyte deployments?
Does the problem also reproduce for other on-prem deployments?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. On affected later OSS deployments, the source page still fails while trying to load the enterprise source stubs.

question_patterns: What exact API request and response do you see when the source page fails?
Can you paste the raw HTTP error for the failing source-definition request?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The request is POST /api/v1/source_definitions/list_enterprise_source_stubs. It returns status 500 with the message 'Internal Server Error: java.io.IOException: HTTP error fetching enterprise sources'.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The enterprise-stubs request succeeds with HTTP 200 and an empty array; the 500 comes from a database migration endpoint instead.
The same endpoint returns the same HTTP-fetch error with a different request ID.

question_patterns: After deleting or restarting the airbyte-server pod, does the source list work?
Please restart the server pod and report only whether the same API error remains.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I deleted the server pods, but the issue still exists on my deployment.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: After the server pod restarted, the source page loaded normally and the error did not return.

edges.comment: Cross-deployment evidence from c11-c14 is explicitly folded into the simulated affected-user side. These are later OSS deployments, not the opening reporter's own cluster. The February Airbyte Cloud registry outage in c9-c10 is excluded because the maintainer explicitly called it a separate problem.

solution.intent: Treat the failure as bad content served by the v0 enterprise connector-stubs endpoint rather than a missing local disable flag: use the reverted endpoint content, restart airbyte-server to clear its cached response, and update Airbyte where possible so endpoint-loading failures no longer block normal webapp use.
solution.concrete_example: The maintainer reported that an incompatible change was accidentally applied to the v0 connector_stubs.json endpoint and then reverted. Restart the airbyte-server pods so they fetch the corrected response instead of retaining cached data. If possible, update Airbyte to a build where failure to load this optional endpoint does not prevent normal webapp use, then verify that source and destination creation works.
solution.inference_hint: The users supplied 403/500 fetch failures and version comparisons, but they did not derive the endpoint defect. The platform maintainer identified that a change had incorrectly been applied to connector_stubs.json on the v0 endpoint, reverted it, and explained that a server restart may be needed to discard cached data.

edges.comment: Accepted technical diagnosis and remediation from c18-c19. The April recurrence is explicitly linked by the maintainer to the earlier cache-related failure class. No affected user subsequently confirmed the corrected endpoint on the opening reporter's deployment, so the terminal state records the maintainer-side correction but remains unverified and user_perceives_resolved is false. The stale-bot closure is omitted as logistics.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted cause as invalid content accidentally served from the v0 connector_stubs.json endpoint, with cached remote data allowing the enterprise-source request to keep failing; it must not diagnose the case solely as a local Helm installation or database problem.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected remote-fetch evidence: connector-registry or compatibility requests return 403, the enterprise-stubs API returns HTTP 500 with an enterprise-source fetch error, and an older chart comparison does not reproduce the problem.

Must explain that the endpoint content was reverted and recommend restarting airbyte-server to discard cached data, while recognizing that a restart alone did not fix every deployment before the remote endpoint was corrected.
Must not present setting ENTERPRISE_SOURCE_STUBS_URL to an empty string as the fix, because the opening reporter already tried that and the errors remained.
Should recommend updating Airbyte where possible so failure to load the optional enterprise-stubs endpoint does not block normal webapp use.
Must ask the affected user to verify source and destination creation after the endpoint correction and server restart, and must not declare the reporter's deployment resolved without that retest.

persona_hint.experience_level: Kubernetes and Helm operator who can deploy Airbyte on-prem, edit Helm values, inspect pod environment variables, collect server logs, test chart versions, and restart pods; not familiar with Airbyte's connector-registry caching internals.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct and concise, with commands and logs when useful; answers deployment-history questions briefly and asks for clarification when a workaround is ambiguous.
